claim: Authors report >95% of their teacher retrieval-heavy performance after preserving ~2% of attention heads in a selected hybrid.
caveat: Retrieval-heavy evaluation, distillation/model selection may not transfer to other tasks.

claim: Olmo 3 published a 7B staged training flow with broad pretraining, targeted midtraining and long-context stage.
caveat: Results are from a full-scale published training recipe, not a small-model replication.

claim: Ai2 reports roughly 2.7× higher training throughput than its earlier MoE stack in a particular eight-B300 comparison.
caveat: Specific hardware, workload and implementation; not a universal MoE multiplier.

claim: DeepSeek-V3 reports approximately 671B total/37B active parameters and 14.8T pretraining tokens.
caveat: Author technical report, not independently reproduced here.

claim: Qwen3 describes switchable think/non-think modes and an inference thinking budget.
caveat: Behavior and token budgets depend on checkpoint/harness; no advantage for our controller proven.

claim: Kimi K2 describes MuonClip stability changes and environment-based posttraining.
caveat: Reported gains cannot be isolated to optimizer without ablations.

claim: Peer-reviewed byteification uses a two-stage retrofit of an existing global subword model into byte-local components.
caveat: Character gains and speed tradeoffs depend on model and evaluation.

claim: Memora's authors report that persistent agent memories often reuse outdated facts during evolving interactions.
caveat: Benchmark covers selected user-like tasks and model samples.

claim: AMA-Bench extends memory evaluation to long-horizon environment/tool trajectories with causal context.
caveat: Study reports specific performance metrics; generalization not established.

claim: Mem2ActBench shows memory-aware agents still struggle to use remembered context to ground tool actions.
caveat: Tasks may reflect synthetic tool and interaction schemes.

claim: Sigma's authors describe a continuous latent diffusion LM warm-started from autoregressive weights.
caveat: Competitive benchmark scores may demand many denoising steps; no speed superiority assumed.

claim: Clock Diffusion proposes block/sliding-window continuous diffusion and caching strategies for language.
caveat: Unclear whether efficient across practical context and batch regimes.

claim: Large empirical study reports that moderate mixes of rephrased synthetic and natural data can help in particular training regimes.
caveat: Optimal ratio depends on budget, model and generator; avoid universal 30% prescription.

claim: Authors describe repetition-aware optimal mixing of limited target-domain data with generic data.
caveat: Tolerance to repetition is source and compute dependent.

claim: A 2026 position paper challenges common broad claims that recursively synthetic training inevitably collapses.
caveat: Position paper reflects one interpretation and does not invalidate other failure conditions.

claim: A 2026 study finds that biased selection/verifier data can suppress rare distribution modes during synthetic data training.
caveat: Depends on assumed data-silo and selection regime.

claim: Ai2 describes auditing approximately 100 models and 34K+ questions to separate benchmark skill dimensions.
caveat: Lab analysis of selected benchmark suite, not proof every capability is measured.

claim: Agent World Model authors describe ~1,000 code/database-backed simulated task environments.
caveat: The number of simulated worlds does not establish cross-domain transfer.

claim: ICLR 2026 RLP explores information-gain-based exploration objectives late in pretraining.
caveat: Improvement may depend on task/data and training compute.

claim: BRIDGE authors report improved mathematical reasoning scores from cooperative SFT/RL optimization.
caveat: Author-reported gains on selected benchmarks, with model and compute confounds to check.

claim: DAPO proposes clipped-policy and sampling modifications for RL on objective reasoning tasks.
caveat: Reported scores are author findings and task/verifier-specific.

claim: Systematic diffusion-LM analysis reports performance changes with denoising steps, blocks and sampling choices.
caveat: Differences need matched end-to-end latency and model weights to attribute to architecture.

claim: Task-sufficient world model study links active probing with structured state discovery.
caveat: Still requires tests on held-out rule and dynamic combinations.

claim: Authors report some reasoning posttraining procedures can reduce the exploration achieved via higher temperature.
caveat: Model and benchmark specific; intermediate-layer decoding may add cost.

claim: v2 full text reports 47/658 PutnamBench problems solved for the 671B model at Pass@1024, whereas the arXiv landing abstract displayed 49/658 at inspection.
caveat: Version and representation mismatch; result remains author-reported and sample-intensive.

claim: Paper v2 documents a Lean 4.9.0 apply? interface bug accepted some invalid 7B apparent proofs; the authors revised earlier success claims.
caveat: Not evidence every remaining result is invalid; demonstrates a checker vulnerability in that setting.

claim: Paper reports 82.4% miniF2F-test Pass@32 and 88.9% Pass@8192 for 671B CoT; these are different sampling budgets.
caveat: Neither number is one-shot accuracy, actual compute cost is not controlled across compared papers.

claim: Free-MAD authors report conformity and majority-vote failure modes and propose scoring full debate trajectories without forced consensus.
caveat: Performance improvements depend on selected models, tasks and cost budgets.

claim: A 2026 multi-agent debate study reports that persuasive incorrect agents degrade aggregate accuracy in its tested setups.
caveat: Adversarial setup is not a universal estimate of failure across all agents.

claim: Neural classifier paper reports miscalibration and benefits of validation-fit temperature scaling in its experimental settings.
caveat: Classification score calibration may fail under domain shifts and does not imply generative answer calibration.

claim: Graph-learning study characterizes graph distinctions that some message-passing GNNs cannot represent.
caveat: Theoretical expressivity bound concerns chosen model classes and is not a global limitation on all AI.

claim: ICLR 2026 speech-language study reports controlled gains from data preprocessing, synthetic data and audio/text sequence composition.
caveat: Study-specific training corpora and models; no reproduction in this repo.

claim: 2026 IJCAI paper proposes separate calibration of retrieved knowledge evidence and downstream reasoning confidence.
caveat: Reported improvements are author-measured on selected knowledge tasks; transfer unproven.

claim: 2026 formal problem-solving paper distinguishes proving a supplied statement from deriving a witness and its proof.
caveat: Automatic evaluation may still depend on formal problem fidelity and tool correctness.

claim: Flow-Lenia authors report raw count and non-neutral evolutionary activity greater in food/dissipative than vanilla, but mass-normalized ranking reverses.
caveat: Raw activity is confounded by differing total matter; these are simulations and neither metric verifies functional heredity.

claim: Flow-Lenia evolutionary experiment uses 500,000 steps, five random seeds, spatial mutation beams and exact parameter vectors as component/species identities.
caveat: Near-identical vectors count as distinct species; phenotype and genealogy are not independently established.

claim: Flow-Lenia OpenES optimization for motion, obstacles and chemotaxis uses externally predefined fitness functions.
caveat: Externally optimized behaviors cannot be credited to an intrinsic no-task evolutionary process.

claim: PBT-NCA v2 explicitly selects worlds under archive descriptor novelty plus DINOv2 visual diversity, with inner gradient objective for territorial aliveness.
caveat: Designer-provided selection signal and visual embedding bias prevent treating chosen morphology as unscripted intrinsic life.

claim: PBT-NCA reports population 30, 500 meta-iterations, 12 inner updates, replacement fraction .25 every five iterations, with three seed runs for reported curves.
caveat: Finite meta-optimization budget and learned world copying are not evidence of independent organism reproduction or indefinite innovation.

claim: PBT-NCA seven-agent condition reports EP near 1 and effective complexity around 0.21±0.05 on its chosen entropy/compressibility metrics.
caveat: Coexistence and spatial pattern scores are metric-dependent and do not demonstrate inherited new ecological functions.

claim: ToLSim evaluates 20 runs of 2 million steps; raw cumulative activity appears unbounded in 8, bounded in 4 and unclear in 8.
caveat: Finite trajectories were classified by sight, so no mathematical claim of infinity or universal system inability follows.

claim: ToLSim gene-component shadow-normalized total and median activity are bounded in all 20 runs and new evolutionary activity is never persistently positive.
caveat: Conclusion depends on gene-valued components, neutral shadow design and selected environment regime; agents/species were not tested as components.

claim: ToLSim neutral shadow model mirrors birth and death counts but chooses random components and periodically resets its state to real population.
caveat: Normalization tests adaptive persistence versus one synthetic neutral process and cannot alone verify ecological new function.

claim: Outlier rule emerged from a genetic-programming search in a 2^140 rotationally symmetric binary CA rule space, using an externally designed novelty score.
caveat: The initial transition physics was externally discovered, even though recurring patterns arise without placing a finished organism.

claim: Original Outlier article reports replications on large sparse grids and a regime change across initial live-cell density thresholds around 0.02 and 0.15 for a 1024x1024 grid.
caveat: Thresholds depend on grid size, environment and finite test configuration; they do not establish robust open-ended heredity.

claim: Outlier clusters repeat around 143 steps and higher-level formations around 1556 steps; the expanding complex ultimately collides or saturates the grid.
caveat: Periodic appearance alone can be an attractor and is not an independently branching offspring lineage under stronger later criteria.

claim: Of 140 rotationally distinct isolated 3x3 Outlier seeds, two join its dominant recurrence trajectory; examined one-bit rule flips did not yield the replication property.
caveat: These are source-reported observations on a selected rule and do not quantify general probability of life-like evolution.

claim: Hintze and Bohm report 15 generations of exact-pattern c2 self-replication in Outlier, using a necessary-cause lineage graph rather than shape resemblance.
caveat: Authors traced a selected deterministic seed, not all rules, and measured exact-copy replication rather than heritable adaptive novelty.

claim: The 2026 follow-up reports a 20,000-tick 1024-square Outlier run producing 31,959,320 cluster instance nodes and 65,552,995 causal edges.
caveat: Large ancestry graph and 966,208 distinct cluster patterns do not alone demonstrate new evolved ecological functions.

claim: Hintze and Bohm report 433 c0 first-generation copies without c0 grandchildren, while c2 exhibits multi-generation branching and distinct temporal pathways.
caveat: Replicator classification is sensitive to specific cluster identity, selected seed, and exact-copy versus functional heredity semantics.

claim: The follow-up identifies c2-like replicators derived from collision debris not on the original c2 lineage, showing recombination of developmental causal routes.
caveat: Authors' new trajectories are not a demonstrated evolving instruction set or adaptation to previously unavailable functions.

claim: The causal lineage tracing includes minimal necessary predecessors for live-cell activations while excluding histories of dead cells.
caveat: Unmodeled negative constraints could alter causal identity in other CA physics; study is not a universal origin-of-life proof.

claim: Stepney's engineering overview proposes autopoiesis, agency and open-ended adaptation as candidate top-level requirements.
caveat: Conceptual framework/requirements, not empirical evidence that a known virtual ALife system satisfies all three or universal agreement.

claim: An ALIFE 2026 late-breaking abstract reports initial Physis automata-chemistry studies where code and language may change, after CPU-to-GPU port.
caveat: The three-page abstract does not establish long-horizon, inherited new operator functions, and no implementation was reproduced here.

claim: Stepney's 2025 complete overview proposes autopoiesis, agency and open-ended adaptation as three high-level engineering requirements, separated from system design and implementation.
caveat: These are author-proposed requirements, not a consensus theorem or empirical demonstration of life.

claim: The 2025 engineering review states that virtual artificial-life systems meeting all proposed full-life requirements have yet to be shown.
caveat: A review's assessment depends on definitional premises, literature coverage and the possibility of partial rather than full life.

claim: Stepney distinguishes variation within a model, innovation changing the model, and transformation changing the meta-model when discussing open-ended novelty.
caveat: The model/meta-model distinction is observer- and representation-relative; it is not a direct measurement of new ecological function.

claim: In a 100-trial parasite-evasion comparison, stochastic-binding Stringmol evaded parasites 32 times, versus zero trials for sticky deterministic-binding Stringmol.
caveat: Study-specific parasite and binding designs; the reported Mann–Whitney QNN p-value evaluates a different outcome statistic.

claim: Stringmol 2016 finds unbound-only decay can select infinite-loop bound molecule complexes that survive without useful ongoing reproduction.
caveat: A modeled decay-regime loophole, not a claim that bound complexes universally dominate chemistry or natural biology.

claim: Length-dependent Stringmol decay can select longer programs and populations whose compute costs become prohibitive for study.
caveat: Author's outcome depends on selected decay rates, sequence representation and simulated population dynamics.

claim: Stringmol UCA authors report 39 viable molecular population takeovers from 500 containers, with 32 involving changes to copier or expressor.
caveat: These are manually identified author experimental events in a hand-seeded artificial chemistry, not replication by AI-Research.

claim: Authors show that changing an expressor can change the meaning of the same genome and yield a viable changed copier, expressor or payload set.
caveat: Changing genomic interpretation demonstrates bounded semantic closure, not independent organismal ecological adaptation.

claim: The 2017 UCA study reports bureaucratic death: proliferation of mutually incompatible expression molecules can collapse otherwise viable replication networks.
caveat: A source-specific system-level failure; the paper does not establish every mutable interpreter is unstable.

claim: The initial 2017 Stringmol UCA requires hand-designed genome, copier and expressor molecules (50 each initially) and an inert HELLOWORLD payload.
caveat: This system is not a de novo artificial protocell; external simulation physics and input state remain crucial.

claim: Physis 2003 evolves interpreter instruction definitions in some offspring, but the original processor structure remains above ninety percent of studied populations.
caveat: Five experiment repetitions and the specified 200k-update horizon cannot prove that structural evolution is impossible.

claim: Physis compares no-external-task reward with an arithmetic-task-reward regime and reports no observed superiority of evolutionary potential versus fixed processors.
caveat: Extra CPU task bonuses are designer-assigned; no observed advantage on these tasks does not settle all potential new environments.

claim: The 2020 Stringmol paper distinguishes type-0 variation within a model, type-1 innovation requiring a revised model, and type-2 emergence requiring a revised meta-model.
caveat: Novelty classification depends on the scientist's chosen starting model and meta-model; this study reconstructs prior observations rather than generating new experimental runs.

claim: Stringmol 2020 calls its reaction-network/hypercycle type-2 novelty EXTRINSIC because the network is added to the observer's scientific meta-model rather than implemented as a new engineering construct.
caveat: An observer's new category is not evidence that a program has internally evolved a new virtual-machine instruction or distinct physical law.

claim: Stringmol 2020 calls several mutation-derived no-product, overwritten-product and multiple-product reaction modes intrinsic model-level innovation.
caveat: Different product outcomes can be a consequence of mutated molecular programs under fixed substrate semantics, not guaranteed adaptive new ecological capabilities.

claim: In the 2020 analysis, reciprocal Stringmol hypercycles require a relation/network-level description: A copies B and B copies A while neither individually copies itself.
caveat: Hypercycle example draws on prior Stringmol studies; the 2020 paper does not report a newly measured rate of network formation or sustained organismal life.

claim: The 2020 Stringmol paper notes that starting with a richer model already containing network interactions changes whether the same observed behaviors qualify as higher-type novelty.
caveat: A model-relative classification must not be treated as an observer-independent measurement of unbounded creative potential.

claim: The authors' ALIFE 2026 abstract reports a Physis CPU-to-GPU port and initial studies of systems whose code and computational language can change.
caveat: Complete three-page conference text and experiment parameters were not reliably inspected here; abstract contains no quantitative results or proof of evolved new ecological functions.

claim: The 2021 spatial Stringmol paper reports 20 runs of which 12 populations had become extinct and eight were still executing at two million timesteps.
caveat: The finite-time survival comparison is author-reported in accessible published summary; no full E2 statistical or code audit in this pass.

claim: Banzhaf and colleagues define open-ended novelty using variation, innovation and emergence levels relative to model and meta-model structures.
caveat: This 2016 paper has only primary abstract and bibliographic verification in this pass; model taxonomy is a conceptual framework, not proof of limitless innovation.
